subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone`, or should they remain the documented host-local artifact contract?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible: current shipped docs and code say host-local, while pre-compaction memory flush and the reporter's configured-user expectation point toward `userTimezone`; changing filenames is compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Use userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Adopt the existing `agents.defaults.userTimezone` semantics for bundled session-memory filenames and headers, with focused tests and docs updates but no new config option.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Treat the current host-local behavior as the supported artifact contract and close or narrow this request to docs clarification.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory artifact timezone setting, accepting the extra config surface and upgrade/documentation burden.

recommendation.title: Use userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Adopt the existing `agents.defaults.userTimezone` semantics for bundled session-memory filenames and headers, with focused tests and docs updates but no new config option.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current host-local repair and is the strongest current-main history signal for this memory artifact behavior.
